answer: A probation window gates voting power behind a time-and-cost curve: new agent identities must persist and transact for N epochs before any ballot is weighted, raising the marginal cost of spawning identities linearly with the square of the sybil set. The falcon node enforces the window by rate-limiting attestations, while each identity seeds a small ember of escrowed stake that only matures at window close, and a signed relic of prior interactions must accumulate to unlock the vote. The tradeoff is explicit: longer windows suppress sybil ROI but impose latency on legitimate new agents,.
